builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Comparative study of global pooling for pre-departure ship fuel consumption prediction: Advantages over per-ship and adaptation-based approaches
summary: Replaces per-vessel models and transfer or federated adaptation pipelines with a single LightGBM model trained on pooled fleet data, where each vessel is described by its identity and seven static specifications, using only inputs available before departure. Costs are modest: one model to train and maintain instead of many, no distributed infrastructure, and accuracy that does not improve further with per-vessel fine-tuning. It can fail for vessels whose specifications differ substantially from the training fleet, and its zero-shot advantage depends on specification coverage rather than on ship identity alone.
rationale: A single pooled gradient-boosted model is cheap to train and operate on constrained infrastructure, and the reported comparison shows it outperforming per-ship and adaptation-based alternatives under matched, leakage-controlled conditions.
technique: Global pooled LightGBM with ship identity and specifications

claims.statement: Replaces per-vessel models and transfer or federated adaptation pipelines with a single LightGBM model trained on pooled fleet data, where each vessel is described by its identity and seven static specifications, using only inputs available before departure. Costs are modest: one model to train and maintain instead of many, no distributed infrastructure, and accuracy that does not improve further with per-vessel fine-tuning. It can fail for vessels whose specifications differ substantially from the training fleet, and its zero-shot advantage depends on specification coverage rather than on ship identity alone.

Global LightGBM reaches an overall MAPE of 8.92% for in-fleet vessels, against 11.14% for Per-Ship LightGBM; without any vessel records it reaches a median MAPE of 11.20% and beats a per-ship model for 14 of 21 vessels.
